title: GfK/NIQ UK Consumer Confidence Barometer — October 2026: the first edition whose fieldwork covers the September policy week, and the last one before the Budget
source: EST: nielseniq.com/global/en/news-center/2026/consumer-confidence-up-one-point-in-september-to-13/, re-fetched direct 2026-10-09 — the September-2026 barometer release lists the remaining 2026 press-release dates verbatim as 'October 23rd, November 20th and December 18th' (all Fridays). That is the THIRD NIQ page carrying the list (the August and July releases, fetched 2026-09-15, carry it too), and the first one written AFTER a listed date was met: the August release's 'September 25th' matched the September edition's actual publication. As with the September edition, the date is the FOURTH Friday, not the third the publisher's landing page gives as its rule of thumb (fetched direct 2026-10-09, text unchanged, and it still publishes no schedule itself) — the dated list is the key, the convention is not. ONE CORRECTION TO THE PROPOSAL: it put the October fieldwork at 'roughly 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-09'. Every October window in the NIQ primaries runs Oct 1-2 to Oct 12-15 (2023 Oct 2-12; 2024 Oct 1-15; 2025 Oct 1-14), so the 2026 survey is IN THE FIELD NOW and should close about 2026-10-14 — the whole September policy week (FOMC 09-16, UK CPI 09-16, BoE 09-17) is BEFORE its start, not inside it. What the edition does carry: UK CPI 3.1% y/y and the BoE's QT retirement as known facts; the 10-01 electricity-VAT change; and the peak of pre-Budget speculation (uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28, five days after publication). The September edition (-13, +1, third straight rise) killed the pre-Budget give-back call: NIQ's commentary named returning inflation, not tax.
